question: Should OpenClaw standardize QA coverage as one exact taxonomy-owned `<surface-id>.<feature-id>` per feature, with scenario definitions—not evidence producers—owning semantic coverage attribution and `smoke-ci` limited to categories demonstrated by its fixed plan?
rationale: The implementation is internally coherent, but the accounting boundary changes report semantics and profile eligibility across the repository; code review cannot determine whether that is the desired permanent QA policy.

options.title: Accept the strict taxonomy contract
options.body: Approve one exact coverage ID per feature and scenario-owned semantic attribution, then merge after the remaining final-head QA checks pass.

options.title: Retain producer-level semantic mappings
options.body: Keep or redesign producer-declared coverage only if QA owners need executable producers to independently define semantic coverage beyond scenario YAML.

options.title: Narrow the policy change
options.body: Split the migration so validation and ownership changes land separately from any contested smoke-profile or report-accounting changes.

recommendation.title: Accept the strict taxonomy contract
recommendation.body: Approve one exact coverage ID per feature and scenario-owned semantic attribution, then merge after the remaining final-head QA checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied final-head history connects this repository member directly to the QA identity and attribution design under review.
